title: Gabber bound for affine opens of an excellent strictly local scheme
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent strictly henselian local scheme of finite Krull dimension $d\geq0$, with $\ell$ invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the ordinary small etale site of $V$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], one has $$H^q(V,M)=0\qquad(q>d),$$ where $q$ is a nonnegative integer and $H^q$ is right-derived global-sections cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No constructibility of $M$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose XV, Corollary 1.2.2, printed p. 219, specialized to an affine open immersion; Expose XVII, proofs of Propositions 3.2.1 and 3.2.2, printed pp. 268–269, affine-open cohomological-dimension input. The result for arbitrary sheaves is the filtered-colimit extension of the constructible assertion.

proof.text: First handle a constructible sheaf. Let $C$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $V$. The affine-open specialization of Gabber’s affine Lefschetz theorem, [lem-per-affine-open-strict-local-cd-constructible], applies to the given Noetherian excellent strictly henselian local scheme $X$, its affine open $V$, the invertible prime-power coefficient ring $\Lambda$, and $C$. It gives $H^q(V,C)=0$ for every $q>d$.

source.place: Expose XV, Corollary 1.2.2, printed p. 219, for the affine open immersion V -> X with delta_X(t) = dim of the closure of {t}, so that f_*delta_X(C) <= d; Corollary 1.2.4, printed p. 220, is its constant-coefficient case.

proof.text: For an arbitrary sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules, [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-colimit-constructible] expresses $M$ as a filtered colimit $M\cong\varinjlim_a C_a$ of constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the qcqs scheme $V$. The hypotheses on $V$ hold because it is affine: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Lemma 03SA (lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible), part (3), applied to the finite ring $\Lambda$.

proof.text: Filtered colimits commute with etale cohomology on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit], so $\varinjlim_a H^q(V,C_a)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(V,M)$ for every $q\geq0$. The module-valued formulation is identified with the underlying abelian-sheaf cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget].
Each $C_a$ is constructible, so Step 1 gives $H^q(V,C_a)=0$ whenever $q>d$. The filtered colimit in Step 3 is therefore zero in those degrees, and hence $H^q(V,M)=0$ for every $q>d$.

source.place: Expose XV, Corollary 1.2.4 together with the filtered-colimit extension used after the constructible assertion.

proof_origin.place: Expose XV, Corollaries 1.2.2 and 1.2.4, printed pp. 219–220, followed by Stacks etale-cohomology Lemma 03SA and Lemma 03Q5 and Sites Lemma 03FD for arbitrary finite-ring module sheaves.
